title: S House / BOV ESTUDIO / BOV ESTUDIO
text:
S House / BOV ESTUDIO / BOV ESTUDIO

In Ayllón (Segovia), adjacent to the historic center, the openings of a 1910 facade now look out onto a courtyard. The facade originally belonged to a family home that was divided into two dwellings in the mid-1940s. Decades later, the owner reunited one of those halves with two adjacent plots to build his primary residence. He wanted a house that could be navigated without steps, and where proximity to the street was compatible with family privacy.

title: Fig Tree House / Estúdio Lava
text:
Fig Tree House / Estúdio Lava

The construction of a residence at Praia da Figueira in Angra dos Reis faced the challenge of being built on a sloped terrain with dense Atlantic Forest vegetation. The semicircular shape stems from the intention to orient the building towards both the sunset and the open sea horizon across the island of Gipóia.

title: Espira Yoga Shala / Arquitectura Mixta
text:
Espira Yoga Shala / Arquitectura Mixta

Inspired by the delicate wings of Costa Rica's glasswing butterfly, Espira explores the relationship between lightness, balance, and suspended movement through a sculptural bamboo structure. Located within the Peninsula Papagayo Sports Complex in Guanacaste, Costa Rica, the Yoga Shala translates these natural qualities into an open architectural form designed to encourage stillness, awareness, and a deeper connection with the surrounding landscape.

title: Intermodal Hub of Lousada / spaceworkers
text:
Intermodal Hub of Lousada / spaceworkers

The planned intervention is located in the northern area of Lousada, a growing zone where new residential clusters, cultural spaces, and an expanded road network are being proposed to integrate with existing infrastructure. The intervention site has a strong cultural dynamic, supported by the Music Conservatory and, more recently, the opening of the Romanesque Interpretation Center. This new cultural hub has contributed to the revitalization of the area and to Lousada's northern expansion, reinforcing its identity as a key cultural district.

title: Verrière House / Projectoire
text:
Verrière House / Projectoire

The project involves the extension of an old barn that had previously been converted into a family residence. Located in Potton, a township bordered to the south by the Canada–United States border and the state of Vermont, the site is bucolic, surrounded by the mountains of the Eastern Townships.

title: Villa Dellago / JM Architecture
text:
Villa Dellago / JM Architecture

Villa Dellago is a private villa located in the natural landscape of the east shore of Garda Lake, in Italy.

title: Argentine Media Library / CONTINUO ARCHITECTURE
text:
Argentine Media Library / CONTINUO ARCHITECTURE

Located in the Argentine neighbourhood of Beauvais, France, the new Argentine Media Library is part of a major urban regeneration programme. Designed by CONTINUO ARCHITECTURE, the project aims to create a new cultural landmark, strengthening the relationship between architecture, public space and community life.

title: Engineered Waterways: What Architecture Can Learn from Urban Canals
text:
Engineered Waterways: What Architecture Can Learn from Urban Canals

Unlike open coastlines or the edges of natural bodies of water, urban canals are narrow, linear, engineered landscapes that cut decisively through the urban fabric. Where rivers follow the contours of a landscape and shape the landform, canals impose their geometry and logic, redefining the relationship between architecture and water. Their edges are clearly defined, often shaped by retaining walls, embankments, and the infrastructure that supports movement along and across the water. Bridges, pedestrian walkways, mooring points, and docks establish a distinctive relationship between the waterway and its context, creating an urban environment where the boundaries between water and architecture are realized.

title: Housing on the Marshes / OFIS Architects
text:
Housing on the Marshes / OFIS Architects

Housing on the Marshes is located along Ljubljana's Path of Remembrance, where the urban fabric meets the landscape of the Ljubljana Marshes. The neighbourhood comprises 170 apartments and two commercial spaces. Its design connects collective housing with planted terraces, shared outdoor areas and a landscape shaped by water, soft ground and a long history of settlement.

title: What Lies Behind the Walls of Contemporary Bathrooms
text:
What Lies Behind the Walls of Contemporary Bathrooms

In 1966, architect and researcher Alexander Kira published "The Bathroom: Criteria for Design", a study that challenged conventional approaches to bathroom planning. Drawing on research into human anatomy, physiology, ergonomics, and personal hygiene practices, Kira questioned whether standardized bathroom fixtures adequately responded to the needs of their users. His work proposed reconsidering these environments through the relationship between the human body and its surroundings, rather than relying exclusively on established dimensions and arrangements.

title: Latin America in Focus: This Month in Architecture, Civic Life, and Heritage Conservation
text:
Latin America in Focus: This Month in Architecture, Civic Life, and Heritage Conservation

This edition of Latin America in Focus explores the ways architecture shapes collective life across different scales and contexts, from public infrastructure and educational environments to the urban histories that continue to inform cities today. The featured projects in Ecuador and Mexico consider how cultural facilities and landscape interventions can support shared activities while responding to their surroundings, while the history of Santo Domingo traces the early development of colonial urban planning in the Americas. The selection also looks at current approaches to cultural heritage conservation and public space, highlighting initiatives in Peru and across the region.

title: The Ribbon / Orms
text:
The Ribbon / Orms

The Ribbon is a new mixed-use development designed by Orms for M&G Real Estate and CBRE Development Management, occupying a prominent corner site at the junction of Oxford Street and Wells Street in central London. The 100,000 sq ft building provides office accommodation above retail space and a basement venue, completing a key gateway site between Oxford Street and Fitzrovia.

title: ZHA’s Recently Completed Théâtre Royal de Rabat in Morocco Photographed by Hufton+Crow
text:
ZHA’s Recently Completed Théâtre Royal de Rabat in Morocco Photographed by Hufton+Crow

The Théâtre Royal de Rabat performing arts complex is located on the left bank of the Bou Regreg River in Rabat, Morocco. Conceived by Zaha Hadid Architects (ZHA) in 2010, it was partially inaugurated in October 2024 and opened to the public on April 22, 2026. The project is part of a cultural development initiative led by King Mohammed VI and stands near the Mausoleum of Mohammed V and the Hassan Tower, a historic minaret. The Royal Theatre of Rabat Foundation oversees the institution's management and its cultural program, which includes concerts, dance, symphony, and theater. A few months after the opening, ZHA has released photography by Hufton+Crow that shows the building's architecture.

title: Caring for Life Across Scales: The XIV Ibero-American Biennial in Brasília
text:
Caring for Life Across Scales: The XIV Ibero-American Biennial in Brasília

Caring for life: this was the motto of the XIV edition of the Ibero-American Architecture Biennial (BIAU) held in Brasília from November 3 to 6, 2026. The choice of care as a theme is significant, as is its presentation as an infinitive verb—lacking tense or mood—serving as an urgent call to action. Structured around the thematic axes of water, vegetation, housing, communities, and new territories, the discussions made it clear that these elements are not mere resources or means for caring for life. Rather, they must be understood as subjects of care, demanding an attentive and respectful consideration of their natural and social cycles within architectural practice.

title: SHISHI Dates Cafe / Naqsh architectural & engineering consultancy
text:
SHISHI Dates Cafe / Naqsh architectural & engineering consultancy

Located within the industrial fabric of Al Quoz, Dubai, SHI SHI brings together the worlds of production, retail, hospitality, and work within a single architectural environment. Designed by NAQSH Architecture, the project explores how the utilitarian character of a factory can coexist with the warmth and intimacy of a café and boutique. Rather than concealing the rawness associated with its industrial setting, the design embraces it as the foundation of its architectural identity.

title: Title Roll Building / Cho and Partners
text:
Title Roll Building / Cho and Partners

The back streets of Sinsa-dong – Sinsa-dong has a strongly commercial character. It was once a quiet area of houses and low-rise multi-unit buildings rather than apartment complexes, with small cafes and shops, but commercial development has gradually taken over. The project sits on a back street between Sinsa and Apgujeong stations, connected to Dosan-daero and very close to the main road.

title: Peacock Forest Retreat / line+ studio
text:
Peacock Forest Retreat / line+ studio

Nestled in a forested valley in northeastern China, Peacock Forest Retreat is a hospitality project that integrates mountain resort experiences with Buddhist rituals and meditation. Designed by line+ studio and completed in March 2023, the project brings together guest accommodation, dining, social spaces, spa and fitness facilities, and contemplative spaces within a continuous architectural and landscape sequence.

title: High Andean Refuge in Quichuay / Pircanato / Pircanato
text:
High Andean Refuge in Quichuay / Pircanato / Pircanato

The High Andean Refuge in Quichuay integrates contemporary materials and production methods with traditional techniques from the Peruvian highlands through an experimental construction system. It is designed to respond to the extreme climatic conditions of the high Andean territory and provide architectural solutions with replicable habitability criteria for rural communities.

title: Modular Bahia / UNA Barbara e Valentim
text:
Modular Bahia / UNA Barbara e Valentim

Between the river and the sea, on the southern coast of Bahia, the Modular Bahia project proposes a contemporary tropical retreat, sensitive to the local territory and climate. Developed by UNA barbara e valentim, the project combines industrialized solutions with bioclimatic strategies - responding precisely to environmental conditions and the desire for a more landscape-integrated occupation.

title: Casa Lucerna / Belen Ilarri Studio
text:
Casa Lucerna / Belen Ilarri Studio

A modest 1970s house had a hidden spatial quality beneath a suspended ceiling.  The intervention begins with this discovery, reorganising the house and recovering a height that completely transforms the perception of space. How can a home be transformed without erasing what makes it unique?

title: The Carmine House / NPS Arquitectos
text:
The Carmine House / NPS Arquitectos

The property consists of a series of platforms that overcome the difference in height between the streets adjacent to the land (approximately 12 metres). On the upper level, there were already some buildings, which appeared somewhat fragmented. The proposal sought to unite these fragments, outlining a U-shape that defines a patio to the east and recovers the old threshing floor to the south/west. The ends of the new shape start at the pre-existing buildings and join to the west with a new body that, while maintaining its shape, stands out for its tectonics.

title: Zunli Tea House / OUT OF OFFICE DESIGN
text:
Zunli Tea House / OUT OF OFFICE DESIGN

Zunli Tea House occupies an old dwelling in Suzhou's historic Gusu district. The owner wanted to bring the intimacy and changing views of a classical Chinese garden into everyday domestic life. A modest budget, restrictions attached to the property's tenancy and the building's fragile condition set clear limits on the renovation. The original room arrangement had to be retained, opportunities for reinforcement were limited, and walls could not be cut into or chased for services. Electrical conduits were therefore surface-mounted, while furniture, planting and finishes became the principal means of reshaping the interior.

title: Fulldraw Winery / Clayton Korte
text:
Fulldraw Winery / Clayton Korte

Fulldraw Vineyard is located within the Templeton Gap AVA, the heart of California's Central Coast wine country. Set on 100 acres of established vineyards, the land is characterized by its rich limestone soils and cool maritime climate—the perfect setting for growing Rhone-style varietals. Tucked into the rolling terrain, the winery is accessed via a long, looping drive taking visitors through the vineyards before arriving at their destination. The proprietors, Connor and Rebecca McMahon tasked Clayton Korte with designing a winery that represents their personality and passion for winemaking. The solution is a winery that is familiar yet exclusive, comfortable yet sophisticated—seemingly disparate ideas that come together through a visitor experience that is as curated as it is intimate.

title: Central Kitchen Graz / Superfuturegroup
text:
Central Kitchen Graz / Superfuturegroup

The new Central Kitchen Graz combines the requirements of a large-scale food production facility with an architectural concept focused on sustainability, circular economy principles, and high-quality working environments. Approximately 15,000 meals are prepared and distributed to municipal childcare facilities and social welfare institutions every day.
